data.content_ref: inline:The claim asserts the theoretical per-period bias (a two-count surplus for residues 0 and 1 over the full 2^31 cycle) will push at least one count outside the 2-sigma window at n=10000. But the covered principle is statistical concentration: at n=10000 the bias per residue class is of order 1 part in ~10^9 relative to the cycle length, an effect utterly negligible compared to the standard deviation of ~37.27. The claim provides no concentration bound, no actual tallies, and no mechanism linking the full-cycle skew to a >2-sigma deviation over a 10000-sample subsequence; it also assumes the subsequence inherits the full-cycle marginal proportion without justification. Thus the conclusion does not follow from the premises: a known full-period bias is not evidence of a 10000-sample outlier within the stated fairness window, and the claimed consequence ('push at least one count outside') is unwarranted without simulation evidence or a variance argument.
